---
title: "Mouse hippocampus (STARmap PLUS)"
---

```{r setup, include = FALSE}
knitr::opts_chunk$set(collapse = TRUE, comment = "#>", cache = TRUE, fig.width = 8, fig.height = 5.5)
knitr::opts_knit$set(root.dir = "/mnt/c/Users/tingthou/Desktop/SIGNAL/SingleCell/RealData")
```

This page analyses spot-level data, where each location has **cell-type
proportions** instead of a single label: STARmap PLUS data of the hippocampus
of a 13-month-old Alzheimer's disease mouse model (Zeng *et al.*, 2023). With
more than 6,000 cells it also shows SIGNAL's settings for large data. To keep
the page quick, it runs three genes named in the paper; the analysis of all
genes uses the same code.

## Data

The processed data used on this page, `starmap_plus_data_use.RData` (counts,
locations and cell-type proportions), can be downloaded from the
[SIGNAL real data folder](https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/1-j6l-KBT9dR_p2RB2RVb_5q9Ig2GdRn3)
on Google Drive. The raw data are sample
`spatial_13months-disease-replicate_1` of study SCP1375 on the Broad Single
Cell Portal. Each segmented cell is treated as a near-cellular spot, and its
cell-type composition is estimated by reference-based deconvolution (CARD
with the DropViz mouse hippocampus reference).

```{r load}
library(SIGNAL)
library(Matrix)
load("starmap_plus_data_use.RData")
dim(data_use$count_use)
prop <- as.matrix(data_use$celltype_proportion)
prop <- prop[, colSums(prop) > 100]       # cell types with enough cells
dim(prop)
round(prop[1:3, 1:5], 2)   # first cells and cell types
```

## Step 1: create a SIGNAL object

Three genes from the paper: *Bin1* and *Apoe*, Alzheimer's disease risk genes,
and *Atp8a1*.

```{r create}
genes <- c("Bin1", "Apoe", "Atp8a1")
obj <- createSIGNALobject(data_use$count_use[genes, ], data_use$location_use, prop)
obj
```

## Step 2: filter and transform

```{r preprocess}
obj <- SIGNAL_preprocess(obj, min_cells = 0, seed = 1)
```

## Step 3: build the kernels

Two of SIGNAL's automatic choices apply:

* **Cell-type kernel:** the cell-type input is a matrix of proportions, so
  SIGNAL uses a Gaussian kernel on the Euclidean distance between proportion
  vectors (`celltype_distance = "auto"`).
* **Spatial kernel:** with more than 6,000 cells, SIGNAL builds one Gaussian
  kernel instead of 11 (`approximation = "auto"`). Its bandwidth is chosen
  from the expression of all genes with Silverman's rule; with only three
  genes in the object, we compute it from the full count matrix and pass it on.

```{r kernel}
bw <- select_bandwidth(data_use$count_use)
bw
obj <- SIGNAL_kernel(obj, bandwidth = bw)
obj@params$kernel[c("celltype_distance", "approximation")]
```

## Step 4: test the genes

Each n × n matrix takes 0.68 GB at 9,244 cells; the main process holds about
20 of them and each parallel worker about 7 more. This page ran on a computer
with 24 GB of memory, so it uses one worker:

```{r test}
obj <- SIGNAL_test(obj, ncores = 1, verbose = FALSE)
signif(obj@result, 3)
```

```{r classify}
res <- obj@result
apply(res[, c("p_celltype", "p_spatial", "p_ctSVG")] < 0.05, 1, function(f)
  paste(c("CellType", "Spatial", "ctSVG")[f], collapse = "+"))
```

Memory needed with more workers:

| Workers (`ncores`) | Memory needed |
|---|---|
| 1 | about 17 GB |
| 8 | about 50 GB |
| 12 | about 70 GB |
| 20 | about 110 GB |

## Step 5: visualise the genes

```{r plot-apoe}
SIGNAL_plotGene(obj, "Apoe", point_size = 0.4)
```

```{r plot-atp8a1}
SIGNAL_plotGene(obj, "Atp8a1", point_size = 0.4)
```
